commit_message:
[Tracy] Bump Tracy to 0.15 (#25241)

Bumps Tracy from wolfpld/tracy@5479a42 (a post-v0.11.1 dev snapshot) to
[v0.15.0](https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy/releases/tag/v0.15.0)
(wolfpld/tracy@f2a4f25).
Upstream changelog:
[NEWS](https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy/blob/v0.15.0/NEWS). Notable
Tracy changes:
- Tracy now also Ships Prebuilt binaries for Linux and Mac (relates to
#19841)
- Loading traces from a URL in the web viewer (relates to #11957)
- Sections and a C API for them (relates to #16051)
- Messages: severity levels and filtering in the GUI
- Bugfixes, e.g. we encountered some use-after-free on Android

Changes apart from the actual bump:
- Message severities: IREE_TRACE_MESSAGE levels now map to Tracy
severities.Colors are unchanged.
- Lock events: the release is now recorded before the unlock
(iree_tracing_mutex_after_unlock → iree_tracing_mutex_before_unlock),
matching upstream. prevents anohter Thread's lock being recorded before
an unlock.
- TracyClient CMake target: IREE sets TRACY_ENABLE ON, because Tracy now
defaults it to OFF. Otherwise the exported target is empty for anything
linking it.
- No system zstd needed for iree-tracy-capture: it's built from source,
and the libzstd-devel installs in the packaging scripts are gone.
- Capture-tool dependencies: capstone moves to 6.0.0-Alpha11 and PPQSort
to 1.0.6, with upstream's patches.

Closes #21371

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[CI] Add LLVMCPU aarch64 and riscv64 lit tests only if LLVM has the target (#25234)

The tests
- early_data_tiling.mlir, early_data_tiling_convolution.mlir,
early_data_tiling_dynamic.mlir, added in
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/24969
- roundeven_native.mlir, added in
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25219 (also riscv64), compile for
aarch64.

byo_llvm.sh builds LLVM with only the X86 target, so iree-compile stops
with "createTargetMachine(...) failed" and the tests fail
linux_x64_clang_byollvm job.

Add these tests in the same way as
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/25221: CMake adds them only if
iree_compiler_targeting_iree_arch() is true for their architecture.

Theaarch64 and riscv64 RUN lines move into *_aarch64.mlir and
*_riscv64.mlir files, which copy the IR.

ci-extra: linux_x64_clang_byollvm

---------

Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: Tag candidate release

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Fold broadcasts into generic contractions too

FoldBroadcastIntoBatchMatmul only matched the named linalg.batch_matmul.
When contractions are generalized earlier in the pipeline
(--iree-opt-generalize-matmul, on from -O2), the contraction is already
a linalg.generic by the time the fold runs, so neither a broadcast nor a
dequantize of a broadcast was folded: the QDQ rewrite then did not see a
dequantize as direct producer and left a float contraction, or the
integer contraction read a materialized batch-sized broadcast.

Add a second pattern for generics that pass the contraction interface.
It reuses the producer matching of the named path, composes the
broadcast into the operand map and leaves the op a generic. The fold is
skipped unless the operand still reads a reduction loop, the new maps
still describe a contraction and every loop is still bound by an
operand. The named batch_matmul path is unchanged.

The stage test gains a run with generalize-matmul=true against the same
integer-path expectations, so broadcast-after-dequantize and
broadcast-before-dequantize weights reach the same form whether or not
the contraction is still named when the fold sees it.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] change pass ordering so img2col convolutions in quantized conv models will result in integer math (#25099)

Addresses https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/25034

Move im2col after the late QDQ conversion and remove the redundant early
QDQ pass, so biased QDQ convolutions convert to integer matmuls after
bias detachment and transpose normalization. Move input demotion
afterward and extend it to generic contractions, preserving f32
accumulation.

Four changes make the single conversion hold up:

- Unit-dim folding shrinks a 1x1 dequantize to rank 0 and leaves an
`expand_shape` between it and the matmul. Reshape fusion by expansion
now handles an empty reassociation for ops without loops, for every op
it supports and in both directions. Only operands that must span every
loop (inits, and the value operand of quantize/dequantize) gain the new
unit dims; scalar parameters stay broadcasts.
- A quantized convolution with a weight zero point needs the sum of
every input window. With QDQ conversion before im2col, that sum
re-gathered every window in its own dispatch and cost about as much as
the im2col itself. The window sum now reads like a ones-filter
convolution, and `ConvertConvToIm2Col` rewrites a convolution without
output-channel reuse when its gather is identical to that of another
rewritten convolution. CSE merges the gathers and the sum becomes a row
reduction over the shared im2col result. Unshared pooling and depthwise
convolutions, dynamic gather shapes and plain matmul sums are
unaffected.
- With im2col after generalization and unit-dim folding, a strided
convolution with a unit window is left with an input access such as `(c,
oh * 2, ow * 2)`, which no longer passes the convolution interface
check. im2col skipped it, and the strided access kept the op from being
data-tiled (the regression reported in review for strided 1x1 shortcut
convolutions). `ConvertConvToIm2Col` now matches on the indexing maps:
an input, a filter and an output, with filter and output maps that are
projected permutations and an input map that is not one but is a sum of
loops scaled by positive constants. Plain contractions, named matmuls
and elementwise ops are left alone; the output-channel reuse and
shared-gather rules are unchanged.
- Unit-dim folding skips named contractions, so the generic that the QDQ
conversion creates from an M = 1 matmul kept its unit loop when
contractions are not generalized. Unit-dim folding now runs on the
function again after the QDQ conversion.

The demotion pass classifies by the contraction and convolution
interfaces and does one rewrite. The multiply-accumulate body check
stays because the convolution interface only inspects indexing maps;
without it a mul+max pooling-like generic would be demoted.

Pipeline regression tests require integer im2col and i8×i8→i32
contractions for biased NHWC/NCHW convolutions, that the window sum
reads the shared gather, and cover generic demotion.

Performance on Apple M4 with llvm-cpu, data tiling and all ukernels,
`--task_topology_performance_level=performance`, median of medians.
NCHW, C_in 16, 28x28 input, C_out 32, activation scale 0.125 and zero
point −1, per-channel weight scale 0.0625 and zero point 2. "Float" is
this branch with `--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false`.

| Case | 1 worker integer | 1 worker float | 4 workers integer | 4
workers float |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3x3 symmetric | 0.103 ms | 0.117 ms | 0.057 ms | 0.062 ms |
| 3x3 activation zero point only | 0.095 ms | 0.118 ms | 0.052 ms |
0.063 ms |
| 3x3 weight zero point only | 0.063 ms | 0.119 ms | 0.042 ms | 0.070 ms
|
| 3x3 both zero points | 0.065 ms | 0.116 ms | 0.041 ms | 0.063 ms |
| 5x5 both zero points | 0.125 ms | 0.241 ms | 0.060 ms | 0.098 ms |
| 7x7 both zero points | 0.197 ms | 0.369 ms | 0.081 ms | 0.194 ms |
| matmul 676x144x32, both zero points | 0.056 ms | 0.149 ms | 0.045 ms |
0.074 ms |

The gather merges for NCHW and NHWC with stride 2, dilation 2 and batch
2. The integer output is bit-identical to the float path on the tested
inputs; the scales are powers of two, so this does not exercise
rounding.

### Comparison against main

`main` at b4f03e34f7 against this branch, same machine and runtime flags
as above, default task topology restricted to the 4 performance cores,
median of 5 repetitions. All cases use
`--iree-global-opt-use-im2col-for-convs`; "DT" adds
`--iree-opt-data-tiling`, "DT + UK" also adds
`--iree-llvmcpu-enable-ukernels=all`. Shortcut cases are 1x1 QDQ
convolutions with bias and relu, written as channels in → out, input
height, stride.

| QDQ case | No DT: main → PR | DT: main → PR | DT + UK: main → PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| shortcut 256 → 512, 56x56, stride 1 | 14.9 → 14.9 ms | 2.35 → 0.79 ms
| 2.38 → 0.79 ms |
| shortcut 512 → 1024, 28x28, stride 1 | 15.9 → 15.9 ms | 2.15 → 0.66 ms
| 2.15 → 0.66 ms |
| shortcut 1024 → 2048, 14x14, stride 1 | 14.2 → 14.8 ms | 2.11 → 0.55
ms | 2.13 → 0.55 ms |
| shortcut 256 → 512, 56x56, stride 2 | 3.99 → 4.26 ms | 0.67 → 0.22 ms
| 0.68 → 0.22 ms |
| shortcut 512 → 1024, 28x28, stride 2 | 5.70 → 6.01 ms | 0.71 → 0.20 ms
| 0.71 → 0.20 ms |
| shortcut 1024 → 2048, 14x14, stride 2 | 4.01 → 4.35 ms | 0.70 → 0.16
ms | 0.71 → 0.16 ms |
| NHWC 1x1, 512 → 1024, 28x28, stride 2 | 0.71 → 1.23 ms | 0.70 → 0.19
ms | 0.70 → 0.19 ms |
| NCHW 3x3, 64 → 64, 56x56, stride 1, pad 1 | 5.20 → 5.56 ms | 0.92 →
0.52 ms | 0.92 → 0.54 ms |

With data tiling these cases take 0.23x to 0.59x of the time on `main`,
because they now run as `i8 x i8 -> i32` matmuls. Without data tiling
the integer matmul is not faster than the float one: most cases are
within 8%, and the NHWC 1x1 stride 2 case is 1.7x slower.

The run covered 237 case and configuration pairs (quantized and float
convolutions, shortcuts, linear layers, each with and without im2col,
data tiling and ukernels). 192 compile to byte-identical modules on both
sides. The other 45 are the 8 QDQ cases above and 7 float convolutions
with bias, in the three im2col configurations; the float ones are within
noise of `main`. No case loses data tiling. The full ResNet-50 from the
review has not been re-measured.

Compiled with:

```sh
build/tools/iree-compile input.mlir \
  --iree-hal-target-backends=llvm-cpu \
  --iree-llvmcpu-target-cpu=host \
  --iree-global-opt-use-im2col-for-convs \
  --iree-opt-data-tiling \
  --iree-llvmcpu-enable-ukernels=all \
  -o model.vmfb
```

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Tile fills to vector sizes like other ops

`LLVMCPUTileToVectorSizePass` skipped every `linalg.fill`, on the assumption
that a fill has already been tiled together with its consumer. An equivalent
`linalg.generic` fill did not get the exemption, so the two forms were handled
differently.

The pass already leaves an op alone when its dimensions are not larger than
the vector sizes, which is the case for a fill that was tiled with its
consumer. Remove the exemption so a fill goes through the same check as every
other op.

that a fill has already been tiled together with its consumer. An equivalent
`linalg.generic` fill did not get the exemption, so the two forms were handled
differently.

The pass already leaves an op alone when its dimensions are not larger than
the vector sizes, which is the case for a fill that was tiled with its
consumer. Remove the exemption so a fill goes through the same check as every
other op.

that a fill has already been tiled together with its consumer. An equivalent
`linalg.generic` fill did not get the exemption, so the two forms were handled
differently.

The pass already leaves an op alone when its dimensions are not larger than
the vector sizes, which is the case for a fill that was tiled with its
consumer. Remove the exemption so a fill goes through the same check as every
other op.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Verify conv decomposition configs on generic convolutions too

`verifyConvTileAndDecomposeExpertConfig` returned early unless the op
implemented `linalg::ConvolutionOpInterface`, and looked up the spatial loops
with a `TypeSwitch` over named ops. A generalized convolution selects the
`ConvTileAndDecomposeExpert` pipeline as well, but skipped this verification,
so a lowering config that is rejected on the named op was accepted on its
`linalg.generic` form.

Match the convolution with `linalg::isaConvolutionOpInterface` and take the
output image and filter loops from `linalg::inferConvolutionDims`. This
verifies named and generic forms alike and no longer needs the per-op layout
table.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Florian Walbroel <walbroel@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Verify conv decomposition configs on generic convolutions too

`verifyConvTileAndDecomposeExpertConfig` returned early unless the op
implemented `linalg::ConvolutionOpInterface`, and looked up the spatial loops
with a `TypeSwitch` over named ops. A generalized convolution selects the
`ConvTileAndDecomposeExpert` pipeline as well, but skipped this verification,
so a lowering config that is rejected on the named op was accepted on its
`linalg.generic` form.

Match the convolution with `linalg::isaConvolutionOpInterface` and take the
output image and filter loops from `linalg::inferConvolutionDims`. This
verifies named and generic forms alike and no longer needs the per-op layout
table.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Handle named and generic convolutions the same in strategy selection

Strategy selection had two checks on `linalg::ConvolutionOpInterface`, which
only named convolution ops implement:

* `getVectorPreProcStrategy` returned `None` for them, and
* `MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::create` skipped lowering config propagation
  to the other ops of the dispatch.

GlobalOptimization generalizes all convolutions, so in the iree-compile
pipeline the root op is a `linalg.generic` and neither check fires. The
checks only made named and generalized forms of the same convolution select
different configurations when the pass runs on named ops directly.

Remove both checks, and drop the `isa<linalg::GenericOp>` condition from the
elementwise/reduction classification in `getVectorPreProcStrategy`, so that
named convolutions take the path the generalized ones already take on every
target.

This does not change what iree-compile generates. Named convolutions fed
directly to the pass now get loop peeling on AArch64 and propagated lowering
configs, like their generalized forms.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Florian Walbroel <walbroel@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Handle named and generic convolutions the same in strategy selection

Strategy selection had two checks on `linalg::ConvolutionOpInterface`, which
only named convolution ops implement:

* `getVectorPreProcStrategy` returned `None` for them, and
* `MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::create` skipped lowering config propagation
  to the other ops of the dispatch.

GlobalOptimization generalizes all convolutions, so in the iree-compile
pipeline the root op is a `linalg.generic` and neither check fires. The
checks only made named and generalized forms of the same convolution select
different configurations when the pass runs on named ops directly.

Remove both checks, and drop the `isa<linalg::GenericOp>` condition from the
elementwise/reduction classification in `getVectorPreProcStrategy`, so that
named convolutions take the path the generalized ones already take on every
target.

This does not change what iree-compile generates. Named convolutions fed
directly to the pass now get loop peeling on AArch64 and propagated lowering
configs, like their generalized forms.

commit_message:
[CI] Call reusable workflows with the self-repository syntax

A `./` path in `uses:` names a file in the runner's workspace. GitHub
resolves the `$/` self-repository form against the workflow's own
repository at the commit that is running, so the reference no longer
depends on what earlier steps put on disk. Policies that require all
actions and reusable workflows to be pinned also count `$/` as pinned.

Switch the reusable workflow calls in ci.yml, pkgci.yml and samples.yml
to `$/`, which fixes the zizmor self-repository findings that failed the
pre-commit hook. The commented-out NVIDIA T4 job and the usage examples
in workflow_summary.yml and the CI docs use the same form, so they stay
correct when copied.

All changed references are job-level reusable workflow calls, which
GitHub resolves before it hands the jobs to runners.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Handle named and generic convolutions the same in strategy selection

Strategy selection had two checks on `linalg::ConvolutionOpInterface`, which
only named convolution ops implement:

* `getVectorPreProcStrategy` returned `None` for them, and
* `MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::create` skipped lowering config propagation
  to the other ops of the dispatch.

GlobalOptimization generalizes all convolutions, so in the iree-compile
pipeline the root op is a `linalg.generic` and neither check fires. The
checks only made named and generalized forms of the same convolution select
different configurations when the pass runs on named ops directly.

Remove both checks, and drop the `isa<linalg::GenericOp>` condition from the
elementwise/reduction classification in `getVectorPreProcStrategy`, so that
named convolutions take the path the generalized ones already take on every
target.

This does not change what iree-compile generates. Named convolutions fed
directly to the pass now get loop peeling on AArch64 and propagated lowering
configs, like their generalized forms.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: pr-greeter

Strategy selection had two checks on `linalg::ConvolutionOpInterface`, which
only named convolution ops implement:

* `getVectorPreProcStrategy` returned `None` for them, and
* `MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::create` skipped lowering config propagation
  to the other ops of the dispatch.

GlobalOptimization generalizes all convolutions, so in the iree-compile
pipeline the root op is a `linalg.generic` and neither check fires. The
checks only made named and generalized forms of the same convolution select
different configurations when the pass runs on named ops directly.

Remove both checks, and drop the `isa<linalg::GenericOp>` condition from the
elementwise/reduction classification in `getVectorPreProcStrategy`, so that
named convolutions take the path the generalized ones already take on every
target.

This does not change what iree-compile generates. Named convolutions fed
directly to the pass now get loop peeling on AArch64 and propagated lowering
configs, like their generalized forms.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
[Docs] Document PyPI trusted publishing in security policy

Updates the security policy for #25204, which publishes stable releases
to PyPI with trusted publishing:

- Verifying release artifacts covers stable wheels, which are attested
  by publish_pypi.yml and carry PEP 740 attestations on PyPI, and shows
  how to verify both kinds of attestation.
- The build and release principles replace the manual PyPI upload with
  trusted publishing and approval through the `pypi` environment.
- Publishing to PyPI without that approval is listed as something to
  report.

commit_message:
[CI] Start the PyPI publish workflow from the stable release tag

Anyone with write access could dispatch the workflow. The `pypi`
environment kept them from publishing, but not from running the
`promote` job, which signs attestations. GitHub cannot limit who creates
releases, but a tag ruleset can limit who creates `v*` tags. Starting
the workflow from that tag push lets the same list decide who can start
it.

The release maintainer names the candidate in the message of the
annotated stable tag. Several nightly candidates can share a commit
(three did for v3.13.0), and anyone with write access can add `iree-*`
tags, so the workflow must not choose one itself.

A patch release rebuilds every package, but only some change. The others
are on PyPI already, and the iree-tools-* wheels have a nightly version,
so only the wheels at the patch version are published, as for 3.7.1.

The workflow now runs as it is at the candidate's commit, so it can only
promote candidates that were cut after it was added.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

Anyone with write access could dispatch the workflow. The `pypi`
environment kept them from publishing, but not from running the
`promote` job, which signs attestations. GitHub cannot limit who creates
releases, but a tag ruleset can limit who creates `v*` tags. Starting
the workflow from that tag push lets the same list decide who can start
it.

The release maintainer names the candidate in the message of the
annotated stable tag. Several nightly candidates can share a commit
(three did for v3.13.0), and anyone with write access can add `iree-*`
tags, so the workflow must not choose one itself.

A patch release rebuilds every package, but only some change. The others
are on PyPI already, and the iree-tools-* wheels have a nightly version,
so only the wheels at the patch version are published, as for 3.7.1.

The workflow now runs as it is at the candidate's commit, so it can only
promote candidates that were cut after it was added.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[CI] Use the workflow token instead of a PAT in release workflows

Replaces every use of the `WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN` personal access token
with `github.token`, scoped per job:

- tag_release (scheduled and one-shot): `contents: write` to push the
  candidate tag and create the draft release, `actions: write` to
  dispatch Build Release Packages.
- build_packages: `contents: write` to upload release assets.
- validate_and_publish / publish_release: `actions: write` to dispatch
  the next workflow, `contents: write` to publish the release and push
  latest-snapshot.
- validate_packages: `actions: read` to download the build artifacts.
- publish_website: `contents: write` to push gh-pages.

`workflow_dispatch` is exempt from the rule that events caused by the
workflow token do not start workflow runs, so the dispatch chain keeps
working. Publishing a release is not exempt, so the publish job now
dispatches publish_website.yml explicitly for non-candidate releases,
mirroring the condition that workflow applies to the `release` event.

The workflow token is minted per job, scoped to this repository, and
expires with the job, so no long-lived credential remains in the
release pipeline.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[CI] Fail zizmor on findings of low severity and above

Informational findings are hints rather than problems, and failing the
Lint workflow on them would block changes without a security gain.

Stop ignoring the self-repository audit for whole files. Its findings
are the `./.github/workflows/...` reusable workflow calls in ci.yml,
pkgci.yml and samples.yml. Until it is decided whether to change these
calls or ignore the audit, the hook reports them and fails.

commit_message:
[Build] Use googletest's gtest_main instead of the compiler copy

Rather than renaming the compiler's copy, delete it. It does what
googletest's gtest_main does, so the compiler unit tests now depend on
@com_google_googletest//:gtest_main. Bazel builds that target from
gmock_main.cc, so bazel_to_cmake.py maps it to googletest's gmock_main
CMake target, and both builds link the same main. With only one
iree/testing package left, compiler/src/CMakeLists.txt no longer needs
to add a directory by hand.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

googletest's gtest_main does, so the compiler unit tests now depend on
@com_google_googletest//:gtest_main. Bazel builds that target from
gmock_main.cc, so bazel_to_cmake.py maps it to googletest's gmock_main
CMake target, and both builds link the same main. With only one
iree/testing package left, compiler/src/CMakeLists.txt no longer needs
to add a directory by hand.

commit_message:
[CI] Use the Azure sccache in the BYO LLVM build

linux_x64_clang_byollvm still reads the GCS ccache. Nothing has written
to that cache since https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/18511 moved
the Linux jobs to the Azure sccache, so every run builds LLVM, MLIR and
IREE from scratch. The scheduled runs take 3 to 5 hours and sometimes
hit the 6-hour job timeout.

Use the Azure sccache with its own key prefix, like the other jobs on
the cpubuilder_ubuntu_jammy image. byo_llvm.sh always passed ccache as
the compiler launcher. It now uses the launcher from the environment if
one is set. LLVM turns off precompiled headers when the launcher is
sccache.

Without the secret, for example in pull requests from forks,
setup_sccache.sh leaves sccache off and the job uses ccache as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

linux_x64_clang_byollvm still reads the GCS ccache. Nothing has written
to that cache since https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/18511 moved
the Linux jobs to the Azure sccache, so every run builds LLVM, MLIR and
IREE from scratch. The scheduled runs take 3 to 5 hours and sometimes
hit the 6-hour job timeout.

Use the Azure sccache with its own key prefix, like the other jobs on
the cpubuilder_ubuntu_jammy image. byo_llvm.sh always passed ccache as
the compiler launcher. It now uses the launcher from the environment if
one is set. LLVM turns off precompiled headers when the launcher is
sccache.

Without the secret, for example in pull requests from forks,
setup_sccache.sh leaves sccache off and the job uses ccache as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: Test TensorFlow / Linux (x86_64)

commit_message:
[CI] Restrict workflow token permissions to read-only (#25207)

Workflows declare no `permissions:` block and `clang_tidy.yml` grants
`contents: write` at the top level. Explicitly set permissions,
restrict/default to read-only.

### Changes

- Add a top-level `permissions: contents: read` to every workflow
- `clang_tidy.yml`: reduce the top-level block to `contents: read`.
cpp-linter runs with `thread-comments: false` and only reads the PR
diff, so it never writes.
- Checkouts that use `WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN` now set `persist-credentials:
false`, so the PAT is no longer written to `.git/config` while `pip
install` and `curl | sh` run in the same job. The two steps that relied
on the persisted credential, the candidate tag push in
`schedule_candidate_release.yml` and `mkdocs gh-deploy` in
`publish_website.yml`, pass the token explicitly instead. The other
pushes already went through `ad-m/github-push-action` with an explicit
token.

### Verification

- `zizmor`: `excessive-permissions` findings 65 → 0

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[CI] Start the PyPI publish workflow from the stable release tag

Anyone with write access could dispatch the workflow. The `pypi`
environment kept them from publishing, but not from running the
`promote` job, which signs attestations. GitHub cannot limit who creates
releases, but a tag ruleset can limit who creates `v*` tags. Starting
the workflow from that tag push lets the same list decide who can start
it.

The release maintainer names the candidate in the message of the
annotated stable tag. Several nightly candidates can share a commit
(three did for v3.13.0), and anyone with write access can add `iree-*`
tags, so the workflow must not choose one itself.

A patch release rebuilds every package, but only some change. The others
are on PyPI already, and the iree-tools-* wheels have a nightly version,
so only the wheels at the patch version are published, as for 3.7.1.

The workflow now runs as it is at the candidate's commit, so it can only
promote candidates that were cut after it was added.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

releases, but a tag ruleset can limit who creates `v*` tags. Starting

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Fold broadcasts into generic contractions too

FoldBroadcastIntoBatchMatmul only matched the named linalg.batch_matmul.
When contractions are generalized earlier in the pipeline
(--iree-opt-generalize-matmul, on from -O2), the contraction is already
a linalg.generic by the time the fold runs, so neither a broadcast nor a
dequantize of a broadcast was folded: the QDQ rewrite then did not see a
dequantize as direct producer and left a float contraction, or the
integer contraction read a materialized batch-sized broadcast.

Add a second pattern for generics that pass the contraction interface.
It reuses the producer matching of the named path, composes the
broadcast into the operand map and leaves the op a generic. The fold is
skipped unless the operand still reads a reduction loop, the new maps
still describe a contraction and every loop is still bound by an
operand. The named batch_matmul path is unchanged.

The stage test gains a run with generalize-matmul=true against the same
integer-path expectations, so broadcast-after-dequantize and
broadcast-before-dequantize weights reach the same form whether or not
the contraction is still named when the fold sees it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Florian Walbroel <walbroel@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[Tracy] Bump Tracy to 0.15 (#25241)

Bumps Tracy from wolfpld/tracy@5479a42 (a post-v0.11.1 dev snapshot) to
[v0.15.0](https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy/releases/tag/v0.15.0)
(wolfpld/tracy@f2a4f25).
Upstream changelog:
[NEWS](https://github.com/wolfpld/tracy/blob/v0.15.0/NEWS). Notable
Tracy changes:
- Tracy now also Ships Prebuilt binaries for Linux and Mac (relates to
#19841)
- Loading traces from a URL in the web viewer (relates to #11957)
- Sections and a C API for them (relates to #16051)
- Messages: severity levels and filtering in the GUI
- Bugfixes, e.g. we encountered some use-after-free on Android

Changes apart from the actual bump:
- Message severities: IREE_TRACE_MESSAGE levels now map to Tracy

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] avoid fusing invariant reduction producers (#25201)

Keep invariant tensor Linalg reductions outside reduction tile loops,
instead of fusing it with the consumer inside the loop, which would
repeat the same computation for each consumer tile. This avoids for
example recomputing whole-row maxima during tiled softmax sums.

IR excerpt of softmax without change (max inside the loop)
```
%15 = tensor.empty(%14) : tensor<?xf32>
%16 = linalg.fill {lowering_config = #iree_cpu.lowering_config<vector_common_parallel = [4]>} ins(%cst : f32) outs(%15 : tensor<?xf32>) -> tensor<?xf32>
%17 = scf.for %arg4 = %c0 to %6 step %c4 iter_args(%arg5 = %16) -> (tensor<?xf32>) {
  ...
  %27 = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d0, d1)>, affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d0)>], iterator_types = ["parallel", "reduction"]} ins(%extracted_slice_6 : tensor<?x?xf32>) outs(%26 : tensor<?xf32>) attrs =  {lowering_config = #iree_cpu.lowering_config<vector_common_parallel = [4, 0], vector_reduction = [0, 4]>} {
  ^bb0(%in: f32, %out: f32):
    %29 = arith.maxnumf %in, %out : f32
    linalg.yield %29 : f32
  } -> tensor<?xf32>
  %extracted_slice_7 = tensor.extract_slice %arg5[0] [%14] [1] : tensor<?xf32> to tensor<?xf32>
  %28 = linalg.generic {...} ins(%extracted_slice_5, %27 : tensor<?x?xf32>, tensor<?xf32>) outs(%extracted_slice_7 : tensor<?xf32>) attrs =  {...} {
  ^bb0(%in: f32, %in_8: f32, %out: f32):
    %29 = arith.subf %in, %in_8 : f32
    %30 = math.exp %29 : f32
    %31 = arith.addf %30, %out : f32
    linalg.yield %31 : f32
  } -> tensor<?xf32>
  %inserted_slice = tensor.insert_slice %28 into %arg5[0] [%14] [1] : tensor<?xf32> into tensor<?xf32>
  scf.yield %inserted_slice : tensor<?xf32>
}
```

With the change:
```
%15 = affine.apply affine_map<()[s0, s1] -> (s0 + s1)>()[%arg2, %arg0]
%extracted_slice_2 = tensor.extract_slice %9[%15, 0] [%14, %6] [1, 1] : tensor<?x?xf32> to tensor<?x?xf32>
%16 = tensor.empty(%14) : tensor<?xf32>
%17 = linalg.fill {lowering_config = #iree_cpu.lowering_config<vector_common_parallel = [4]>} ins(%cst_0 : f32) outs(%16 : tensor<?xf32>) -> tensor<?xf32>
%18 = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d0, d1)>, affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d0)>], iterator_types = ["parallel", "reduction"]} ins(%extracted_slice_2 : tensor<?x?xf32>) outs(%17 : tensor<?xf32>) attrs =  {lowering_config = #iree_cpu.lowering_config<vector_common_parallel = [4, 0], vector_reduction = [0, 4]>} {
^bb0(%in: f32, %out: f32):
  %26 = arith.maxnumf %in, %out : f32
  linalg.yield %26 : f32
} -> tensor<?xf32>
%19 = tensor.empty(%14) : tensor<?xf32>
%20 = linalg.fill {lowering_config = #iree_cpu.lowering_config<vector_common_parallel = [4]>} ins(%cst : f32) outs(%19 : tensor<?xf32>) -> tensor<?xf32>
%21 = scf.for %arg4 = %c0 to %6 step %c4 iter_args(%arg5 = %20) -> (tensor<?xf32>) {
  ...
  %28 = linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d0, d1)>, affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d0)>, affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d0)>], iterator_types = ["parallel", "reduction"]} ins(%extracted_slice_6, %extracted_slice_7 : tensor<?x?xf32>, tensor<?xf32>) outs(%extracted_slice_8 : tensor<?xf32>) attrs =  {lowering_config = #iree_cpu.lowering_config<distribution = [32, 0], vector_common_parallel = [4, 0], vector_reduction = [0, 4]>} {
  ^bb0(%in: f32, %in_9: f32, %out: f32):
    %29 = arith.subf %in, %in_9 : f32
    %30 = math.exp %29 : f32
    %31 = arith.addf %30, %out : f32
    linalg.yield %31 : f32
  } -> tensor<?xf32>
  %inserted_slice = tensor.insert_slice %28 into %arg5[0] [%14] [1] : tensor<?xf32> into tensor<?xf32>
  scf.yield %inserted_slice : tensor<?xf32>
}
```

LICM does not move the max out of the loop because it only runs after
the max computation has been tiled, at which point LICM cannot prove
invariance anymore.

commit_message:
[CI] Restrict workflow token permissions to read-only (#25207)

Workflows declare no `permissions:` block and `clang_tidy.yml` grants
`contents: write` at the top level. Explicitly set permissions,
restrict/default to read-only.

### Changes

- Add a top-level `permissions: contents: read` to every workflow
- `clang_tidy.yml`: reduce the top-level block to `contents: read`.
cpp-linter runs with `thread-comments: false` and only reads the PR
diff, so it never writes.
- Checkouts that use `WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN` now set `persist-credentials:
false`, so the PAT is no longer written to `.git/config` while `pip
install` and `curl | sh` run in the same job. The two steps that relied
on the persisted credential, the candidate tag push in
`schedule_candidate_release.yml` and `mkdocs gh-deploy` in
`publish_website.yml`, pass the token explicitly instead. The other
pushes already went through `ad-m/github-push-action` with an explicit
token.

### Verification

- `zizmor`: `excessive-permissions` findings 65 → 0

commit_message:
[CI] Use the Azure sccache in the BYO LLVM build

linux_x64_clang_byollvm still reads the GCS ccache. Nothing has written
to that cache since https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/18511 moved
the Linux jobs to the Azure sccache, so every run builds LLVM, MLIR and
IREE from scratch. The scheduled runs take 3 to 5 hours and sometimes
hit the 6-hour job timeout.

Use the Azure sccache with its own key prefix, like the other jobs on
the cpubuilder_ubuntu_jammy image. byo_llvm.sh always passed ccache as
the compiler launcher. It now uses the launcher from the environment if
one is set. LLVM turns off precompiled headers when the launcher is
sccache.

Without the secret, for example in pull requests from forks,
setup_sccache.sh leaves sccache off and the job uses ccache as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

linux_x64_clang_byollvm still reads the GCS ccache. Nothing has written
to that cache since https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/18511 moved
the Linux jobs to the Azure sccache, so every run builds LLVM, MLIR and
IREE from scratch. The scheduled runs take 3 to 5 hours and sometimes
hit the 6-hour job timeout.

Use the Azure sccache with its own key prefix, like the other jobs on
the cpubuilder_ubuntu_jammy image. byo_llvm.sh always passed ccache as
the compiler launcher. It now uses the launcher from the environment if
one is set. LLVM turns off precompiled headers when the launcher is
sccache.

Without the secret, for example in pull requests from forks,
setup_sccache.sh leaves sccache off and the job uses ccache as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: pkgci_summary / summary

commit_message:
[Build] Use googletest's gtest_main instead of the compiler copy

Rather than renaming the compiler's copy, delete it. It does what
googletest's gtest_main does, so the compiler unit tests now depend on
@com_google_googletest//:gtest_main. Bazel builds that target from
gmock_main.cc, so bazel_to_cmake.py maps it to googletest's gmock_main
CMake target, and both builds link the same main. With only one
iree/testing package left, compiler/src/CMakeLists.txt no longer needs
to add a directory by hand.

commit_message:
[CI] Use the workflow token instead of a PAT in release workflows

Replaces every use of the `WRITE_ACCESS_TOKEN` personal access token
with `github.token`, scoped per job:

- tag_release (scheduled and one-shot): `contents: write` to push the
  candidate tag and create the draft release, `actions: write` to
  dispatch Build Release Packages.
- build_packages: `contents: write` to upload release assets.
- validate_and_publish / publish_release: `actions: write` to dispatch
  the next workflow, `contents: write` to publish the release and push
  latest-snapshot.
- validate_packages: `actions: read` to download the build artifacts.
- publish_website: `contents: write` to push gh-pages.

`workflow_dispatch` is exempt from the rule that events caused by the
workflow token do not start workflow runs, so the dispatch chain keeps
working. Publishing a release is not exempt, so the publish job now
dispatches publish_website.yml explicitly for non-candidate releases,
mirroring the condition that workflow applies to the `release` event.

The workflow token is minted per job, scoped to this repository, and
expires with the job, so no long-lived credential remains in the
release pipeline.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: Test ONNX / test_onnx_ops :: amdgpu_vulkan_rdna3_O0

commit_message:
[CI] Start the PyPI publish workflow from the stable release tag

Anyone with write access could dispatch the workflow. The `pypi`
environment kept them from publishing, but not from running the
`promote` job, which signs attestations. GitHub cannot limit who creates
releases, but a tag ruleset can limit who creates `v*` tags. Starting
the workflow from that tag push lets the same list decide who can start
it.

The release maintainer names the candidate in the message of the
annotated stable tag. Several nightly candidates can share a commit
(three did for v3.13.0), and anyone with write access can add `iree-*`
tags, so the workflow must not choose one itself.

A patch release rebuilds every package, but only some change. The others
are on PyPI already, and the iree-tools-* wheels have a nightly version,
so only the wheels at the patch version are published, as for 3.7.1.

The workflow now runs as it is at the candidate's commit, so it can only
promote candidates that were cut after it was added.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
name: Test ONNX / test_onnx_ops :: amdgpu_hip_rdna4_O3

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Handle named and generic convolutions the same in strategy selection

Strategy selection had two checks on `linalg::ConvolutionOpInterface`, which
only named convolution ops implement:

* `getVectorPreProcStrategy` returned `None` for them, and
* `MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::create` skipped lowering config propagation
  to the other ops of the dispatch.

GlobalOptimization generalizes all convolutions, so in the iree-compile
pipeline the root op is a `linalg.generic` and neither check fires. The
checks only made named and generalized forms of the same convolution select
different configurations when the pass runs on named ops directly.

Remove both checks, and drop the `isa<linalg::GenericOp>` condition from the
elementwise/reduction classification in `getVectorPreProcStrategy`, so that
named convolutions take the path the generalized ones already take on every
target.

This does not change what iree-compile generates. Named convolutions fed
directly to the pass now get loop peeling on AArch64 and propagated lowering
configs, like their generalized forms.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Florian Walbroel <walbroel@roofline.ai>
name: Test Torch / test_torch_ops :: amdgpu_hip_gfx1201_O3

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Verify conv decomposition configs on generic convolutions too

`verifyConvTileAndDecomposeExpertConfig` returned early unless the op
implemented `linalg::ConvolutionOpInterface`, and looked up the spatial loops
with a `TypeSwitch` over named ops. A generalized convolution selects the
`ConvTileAndDecomposeExpert` pipeline as well, but skipped this verification,
so a lowering config that is rejected on the named op was accepted on its
`linalg.generic` form.

Match the convolution with `linalg::isaConvolutionOpInterface` and take the
output image and filter loops from `linalg::inferConvolutionDims`. This
verifies named and generic forms alike and no longer needs the per-op layout
table.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Florian Walbroel <walbroel@roofline.ai>
name: Test Torch / test_torch_ops :: amdgpu_hip_gfx1201_O3

verifies named and generic forms alike and no longer needs the per-op layout
table.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Tile fills to vector sizes like other ops

`LLVMCPUTileToVectorSizePass` skipped every `linalg.fill`, on the assumption
that a fill has already been tiled together with its consumer. An equivalent
`linalg.generic` fill did not get the exemption, so the two forms were handled
differently.

The pass already leaves an op alone when its dimensions are not larger than
the vector sizes, which is the case for a fill that was tiled with its
consumer. Remove the exemption so a fill goes through the same check as every
other op.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] change pass ordering so img2col convolutions in quantized conv models will result in integer math (#25099)

Addresses https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/25034

Move im2col after the late QDQ conversion and remove the redundant early
QDQ pass, so biased QDQ convolutions convert to integer matmuls after
bias detachment and transpose normalization. Move input demotion
afterward and extend it to generic contractions, preserving f32
accumulation.

Four changes make the single conversion hold up:

- Unit-dim folding shrinks a 1x1 dequantize to rank 0 and leaves an
`expand_shape` between it and the matmul. Reshape fusion by expansion
now handles an empty reassociation for ops without loops, for every op
it supports and in both directions. Only operands that must span every
loop (inits, and the value operand of quantize/dequantize) gain the new
unit dims; scalar parameters stay broadcasts.
- A quantized convolution with a weight zero point needs the sum of
every input window. With QDQ conversion before im2col, that sum
re-gathered every window in its own dispatch and cost about as much as
the im2col itself. The window sum now reads like a ones-filter
convolution, and `ConvertConvToIm2Col` rewrites a convolution without
output-channel reuse when its gather is identical to that of another
rewritten convolution. CSE merges the gathers and the sum becomes a row
reduction over the shared im2col result. Unshared pooling and depthwise
convolutions, dynamic gather shapes and plain matmul sums are
unaffected.
- With im2col after generalization and unit-dim folding, a strided
convolution with a unit window is left with an input access such as `(c,
oh * 2, ow * 2)`, which no longer passes the convolution interface
check. im2col skipped it, and the strided access kept the op from being
data-tiled (the regression reported in review for strided 1x1 shortcut
convolutions). `ConvertConvToIm2Col` now matches on the indexing maps:
an input, a filter and an output, with filter and output maps that are
projected permutations and an input map that is not one but is a sum of
loops scaled by positive constants. Plain contractions, named matmuls
and elementwise ops are left alone; the output-channel reuse and
shared-gather rules are unchanged.
- Unit-dim folding skips named contractions, so the generic that the QDQ
conversion creates from an M = 1 matmul kept its unit loop when
contractions are not generalized. Unit-dim folding now runs on the
function again after the QDQ conversion.

The demotion pass classifies by the contraction and convolution
interfaces and does one rewrite. The multiply-accumulate body check
stays because the convolution interface only inspects indexing maps;
without it a mul+max pooling-like generic would be demoted.

Pipeline regression tests require integer im2col and i8×i8→i32
contractions for biased NHWC/NCHW convolutions, that the window sum
reads the shared gather, and cover generic demotion.

Performance on Apple M4 with llvm-cpu, data tiling and all ukernels,
`--task_topology_performance_level=performance`, median of medians.
NCHW, C_in 16, 28x28 input, C_out 32, activation scale 0.125 and zero
point −1, per-channel weight scale 0.0625 and zero point 2. "Float" is
this branch with `--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false`.

| Case | 1 worker integer | 1 worker float | 4 workers integer | 4
workers float |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3x3 symmetric | 0.103 ms | 0.117 ms | 0.057 ms | 0.062 ms |
| 3x3 activation zero point only | 0.095 ms | 0.118 ms | 0.052 ms |
0.063 ms |
| 3x3 weight zero point only | 0.063 ms | 0.119 ms | 0.042 ms | 0.070 ms
|
| 3x3 both zero points | 0.065 ms | 0.116 ms | 0.041 ms | 0.063 ms |
| 5x5 both zero points | 0.125 ms | 0.241 ms | 0.060 ms | 0.098 ms |
| 7x7 both zero points | 0.197 ms | 0.369 ms | 0.081 ms | 0.194 ms |
| matmul 676x144x32, both zero points | 0.056 ms | 0.149 ms | 0.045 ms |
0.074 ms |

The gather merges for NCHW and NHWC with stride 2, dilation 2 and batch
2. The integer output is bit-identical to the float path on the tested
inputs; the scales are powers of two, so this does not exercise
rounding.

### Comparison against main

`main` at b4f03e34f7 against this branch, same machine and runtime flags
as above, default task topology restricted to the 4 performance cores,
median of 5 repetitions. All cases use
`--iree-global-opt-use-im2col-for-convs`; "DT" adds
`--iree-opt-data-tiling`, "DT + UK" also adds
`--iree-llvmcpu-enable-ukernels=all`. Shortcut cases are 1x1 QDQ
convolutions with bias and relu, written as channels in → out, input
height, stride.

| QDQ case | No DT: main → PR | DT: main → PR | DT + UK: main → PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| shortcut 256 → 512, 56x56, stride 1 | 14.9 → 14.9 ms | 2.35 → 0.79 ms
| 2.38 → 0.79 ms |
| shortcut 512 → 1024, 28x28, stride 1 | 15.9 → 15.9 ms | 2.15 → 0.66 ms
| 2.15 → 0.66 ms |
| shortcut 1024 → 2048, 14x14, stride 1 | 14.2 → 14.8 ms | 2.11 → 0.55
ms | 2.13 → 0.55 ms |
| shortcut 256 → 512, 56x56, stride 2 | 3.99 → 4.26 ms | 0.67 → 0.22 ms
| 0.68 → 0.22 ms |
| shortcut 512 → 1024, 28x28, stride 2 | 5.70 → 6.01 ms | 0.71 → 0.20 ms
| 0.71 → 0.20 ms |
| shortcut 1024 → 2048, 14x14, stride 2 | 4.01 → 4.35 ms | 0.70 → 0.16
ms | 0.71 → 0.16 ms |
| NHWC 1x1, 512 → 1024, 28x28, stride 2 | 0.71 → 1.23 ms | 0.70 → 0.19
ms | 0.70 → 0.19 ms |
| NCHW 3x3, 64 → 64, 56x56, stride 1, pad 1 | 5.20 → 5.56 ms | 0.92 →
0.52 ms | 0.92 → 0.54 ms |

With data tiling these cases take 0.23x to 0.59x of the time on `main`,
because they now run as `i8 x i8 -> i32` matmuls. Without data tiling
the integer matmul is not faster than the float one: most cases are
within 8%, and the NHWC 1x1 stride 2 case is 1.7x slower.

The run covered 237 case and configuration pairs (quantized and float
convolutions, shortcuts, linear layers, each with and without im2col,
data tiling and ukernels). 192 compile to byte-identical modules on both
sides. The other 45 are the 8 QDQ cases above and 7 float convolutions
with bias, in the three im2col configurations; the float ones are within
noise of `main`. No case loses data tiling. The full ResNet-50 from the
review has not been re-measured.

Compiled with:

```sh
build/tools/iree-compile input.mlir \
  --iree-hal-target-backends=llvm-cpu \
  --iree-llvmcpu-target-cpu=host \
  --iree-global-opt-use-im2col-for-convs \
  --iree-opt-data-tiling \
  --iree-llvmcpu-enable-ukernels=all \
  -o model.vmfb
```

[GlobalOptimization] change pass ordering so img2col convolutions in quantized conv models will result in integer math (#25099)

Addresses https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/25034

Move im2col after the late QDQ conversion and remove the redundant early
QDQ pass, so biased QDQ convolutions convert to integer matmuls after
bias detachment and transpose normalization. Move input demotion
afterward and extend it to generic contractions, preserving f32
accumulation.

Four changes make the single conversion hold up:

- Unit-dim folding shrinks a 1x1 dequantize to rank 0 and leaves an
`expand_shape` between it and the matmul. Reshape fusion by expansion
now handles an empty reassociation for ops without loops, for every op
it supports and in both directions. Only operands that must span every
loop (inits, and the value operand of quantize/dequantize) gain the new
unit dims; scalar parameters stay broadcasts.
- A quantized convolution with a weight zero point needs the sum of
every input window. With QDQ conversion before im2col, that sum
re-gathered every window in its own dispatch and cost about as much as
the im2col itself. The window sum now reads like a ones-filter
convolution, and `ConvertConvToIm2Col` rewrites a convolution without
output-channel reuse when its gather is identical to that of another
rewritten convolution. CSE merges the gathers and the sum becomes a row
reduction over the shared im2col result. Unshared pooling and depthwise
convolutions, dynamic gather shapes and plain matmul sums are
unaffected.
- With im2col after generalization and unit-dim folding, a strided
convolution with a unit window is left with an input access such as `(c,
oh * 2, ow * 2)`, which no longer passes the convolution interface
check. im2col skipped it, and the strided access kept the op from being
data-tiled (the regression reported in review for strided 1x1 shortcut
convolutions). `ConvertConvToIm2Col` now matches on the indexing maps:
an input, a filter and an output, with filter and output maps that are
projected permutations and an input map that is not one but is a sum of
loops scaled by positive constants. Plain contractions, named matmuls
and elementwise ops are left alone; the output-channel reuse and
shared-gather rules are unchanged.
- Unit-dim folding skips named contractions, so the generic that the QDQ
conversion creates from an M = 1 matmul kept its unit loop when
contractions are not generalized. Unit-dim folding now runs on the
function again after the QDQ conversion.

The demotion pass classifies by the contraction and convolution
interfaces and does one rewrite. The multiply-accumulate body check
stays because the convolution interface only inspects indexing maps;
without it a mul+max pooling-like generic would be demoted.

Pipeline regression tests require integer im2col and i8×i8→i32
contractions for biased NHWC/NCHW convolutions, that the window sum
reads the shared gather, and cover generic demotion.

Performance on Apple M4 with llvm-cpu, data tiling and all ukernels,
`--task_topology_performance_level=performance`, median of medians.
NCHW, C_in 16, 28x28 input, C_out 32, activation scale 0.125 and zero
point −1, per-channel weight scale 0.0625 and zero point 2. "Float" is
this branch with `--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false`.

| Case | 1 worker integer | 1 worker float | 4 workers integer | 4
workers float |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3x3 symmetric | 0.103 ms | 0.117 ms | 0.057 ms | 0.062 ms |
| 3x3 activation zero point only | 0.095 ms | 0.118 ms | 0.052 ms |
0.063 ms |
| 3x3 weight zero point only | 0.063 ms | 0.119 ms | 0.042 ms | 0.070 ms
|
| 3x3 both zero points | 0.065 ms | 0.116 ms | 0.041 ms | 0.063 ms |
| 5x5 both zero points | 0.125 ms | 0.241 ms | 0.060 ms | 0.098 ms |
| 7x7 both zero points | 0.197 ms | 0.369 ms | 0.081 ms | 0.194 ms |
| matmul 676x144x32, both zero points | 0.056 ms | 0.149 ms | 0.045 ms |
0.074 ms |

inputs; the scales are powers of two, so this does not exercise
rounding.

`main` at b4f03e34f7 against this branch, same machine and runtime flags

median of 5 repetitions. All cases use
`--iree-global-opt-use-im2col-for-convs`; "DT" adds
`--iree-opt-data-tiling`, "DT + UK" also adds
`--iree-llvmcpu-enable-ukernels=all`. Shortcut cases are 1x1 QDQ
convolutions with bias and relu, written as channels in → out, input
height, stride.

| QDQ case | No DT: main → PR | DT: main → PR | DT + UK: main → PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| shortcut 256 → 512, 56x56, stride 1 | 14.9 → 14.9 ms | 2.35 → 0.79 ms
| 2.38 → 0.79 ms |
| shortcut 512 → 1024, 28x28, stride 1 | 15.9 → 15.9 ms | 2.15 → 0.66 ms
| 2.15 → 0.66 ms |
| shortcut 1024 → 2048, 14x14, stride 1 | 14.2 → 14.8 ms | 2.11 → 0.55
ms | 2.13 → 0.55 ms |
| shortcut 256 → 512, 56x56, stride 2 | 3.99 → 4.26 ms | 0.67 → 0.22 ms
| 0.68 → 0.22 ms |
| shortcut 512 → 1024, 28x28, stride 2 | 5.70 → 6.01 ms | 0.71 → 0.20 ms
| 0.71 → 0.20 ms |
| shortcut 1024 → 2048, 14x14, stride 2 | 4.01 → 4.35 ms | 0.70 → 0.16
ms | 0.71 → 0.16 ms |
| NHWC 1x1, 512 → 1024, 28x28, stride 2 | 0.71 → 1.23 ms | 0.70 → 0.19
ms | 0.70 → 0.19 ms |
| NCHW 3x3, 64 → 64, 56x56, stride 1, pad 1 | 5.20 → 5.56 ms | 0.92 →
0.52 ms | 0.92 → 0.54 ms |

noise of `main`. No case loses data tiling. The full ResNet-50 from the
review has not been re-measured.

```sh
  --iree-hal-target-backends=llvm-cpu \
  --iree-llvmcpu-target-cpu=host \
  --iree-global-opt-use-im2col-for-convs \
  --iree-opt-data-tiling \
  --iree-llvmcpu-enable-ukernels=all \
  -o model.vmfb
```

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Fold broadcasts into generic contractions too

FoldBroadcastIntoBatchMatmul only matched the named linalg.batch_matmul.
When contractions are generalized earlier in the pipeline
(--iree-opt-generalize-matmul, on from -O2), the contraction is already
a linalg.generic by the time the fold runs, so neither a broadcast nor a
dequantize of a broadcast was folded: the QDQ rewrite then did not see a
dequantize as direct producer and left a float contraction, or the
integer contraction read a materialized batch-sized broadcast.

Add a second pattern for generics that pass the contraction interface.
It reuses the producer matching of the named path, composes the
broadcast into the operand map and leaves the op a generic. The fold is
skipped unless the operand still reads a reduction loop, the new maps
still describe a contraction and every loop is still bound by an
operand. The named batch_matmul path is unchanged.

The stage test gains a run with generalize-matmul=true against the same
integer-path expectations, so broadcast-after-dequantize and
broadcast-before-dequantize weights reach the same form whether or not
the contraction is still named when the fold sees it.

commit_message:
[GlobalOpt] Fold broadcasts into generic contractions too

FoldBroadcastIntoBatchMatmul only matched the named linalg.batch_matmul.
When contractions are generalized earlier in the pipeline
(--iree-opt-generalize-matmul, on from -O2), the contraction is already
a linalg.generic by the time the fold runs, so neither a broadcast nor a
dequantize of a broadcast was folded: the QDQ rewrite then did not see a
dequantize as direct producer and left a float contraction, or the
integer contraction read a materialized batch-sized broadcast.

Add a second pattern for generics that pass the contraction interface.
It reuses the producer matching of the named path, composes the
broadcast into the operand map and leaves the op a generic. The fold is
skipped unless the operand still reads a reduction loop, the new maps
still describe a contraction and every loop is still bound by an
operand. The named batch_matmul path is unchanged.

The stage test gains a run with generalize-matmul=true against the same
integer-path expectations, so broadcast-after-dequantize and
broadcast-before-dequantize weights reach the same form whether or not
the contraction is still named when the fold sees it.
